root_cause.text: The wave5 VPU driver’s runtime-PM/autosuspend handling was tied to open/close instance lifetime incorrectly, so the device could autosuspend while a decoder buffer queue path still accessed hardware registers in `wave5_dec_clr_disp_flag()`, triggering an SError on closed/idle transitions.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes `pm_runtime_use_autosuspend()` from the first-open path and `pm_runtime_dont_use_autosuspend()` from close, and adds `pm_runtime_resume_and_get()`/`pm_runtime_put_autosuspend()` around `wave5_vpu_dec_buf_queue_dst()`; the commit message explicitly says the panic happened because “timeout of autosuspend delay happened” and the device entered suspend mode.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The wave5 VPU driver’s runtime-PM/autosuspend handling was tied to open/close instance lifetime incorrectly, so the device could autosuspend while a decoder buffer queue path still accessed hardware registers in `wave5_dec_clr_disp_flag()`, triggering an SError on closed/idle transitions.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch removes `pm_runtime_use_autosuspend()` from the first-open path and `pm_runtime_dont_use_autosuspend()` from close, and adds `pm_runtime_resume_and_get()`/`pm_runtime_put_autosuspend()` around `wave5_vpu_dec_buf_queue_dst()`; the commit message explicitly says the panic happened because “timeout of autosuspend delay happened” and the device entered suspend mode.

intent_record.intent_summary: Resume the VPU device on destination buffer queue to ensure decoding buffer handling occurs while the device is powered.
intent_record.what: A call to `pm_runtime_resume_and_get(inst->dev->dev);` was inserted at the start of `wave5_vpu_dec_buf_queue_dst(struct vb2_buffer *vb)`, before `vbuf->sequence` is assigned and before the existing state check.
intent_record.how: When a destination buffer is queued, the device is now explicitly resumed and its runtime PM usage count is incremented before further processing. This ensures the VPU device is powered on/available while handling queued decode buffers, preventing operations from running against a suspended device.

intent_record.intent_summary: Release the runtime PM reference after queuing a destination buffer so the device can autosuspend correctly.
intent_record.what: A single new call to `pm_runtime_put_autosuspend(inst->dev->dev);` was added at the end of `wave5_vpu_dec_buf_queue_dst(struct vb2_buffer *vb)`, after the existing buffer-queueing logic.
intent_record.how: After a destination buffer is queued, the device runtime PM reference is now released and the device is allowed to autosuspend when idle. This prevents the VPU from staying unnecessarily active after queueing completes and helps balance the earlier runtime resume/get usage.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the first-instance autosuspend activation from decoder open handling.
intent_record.what: The code removes a conditional block in `wave5_vpu_open_dec()` that checked `if (list_empty(&dev->instances))` and called `pm_runtime_use_autosuspend(inst->dev->dev);` before adding the new instance to `dev->instances`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function no longer enables autosuspend only when the first decoder instance is opened, so the device will not switch runtime PM behavior at this point in the open path. This changes the power-management setup that previously occurred on the transition from zero to one instances.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the one-time autosuspend setup from encoder open so instance registration proceeds without altering runtime PM behavior here.
intent_record.what: The code removed an `if (list_empty(&dev->instances)) pm_runtime_use_autosuspend(inst->dev->dev);` block from `wave5_vpu_open_enc()`, so the function now goes directly from a successful setup to `list_add_tail(&inst->list, &dev->instances);`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the first encoder instance no longer enables runtime PM autosuspend only when the instance list is empty. This changes when autosuspend policy is configured during encoder open, preventing that one-time conditional call from being made in this path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Increase the VPU runtime PM autosuspend delay from 100 to 500 to avoid suspending the device too aggressively.
intent_record.what: In wave5_vpu_probe(), the runtime PM autosuspend delay passed to pm_runtime_set_autosuspend_delay() was changed from 100 to 500.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the device will now remain active for a longer period of inactivity before autosuspending, reducing how quickly the VPU enters low-power suspend after probe and early use.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove unused local variables from wave5_vpu_dec_close() to clean up the function.
intent_record.what: Two local variables were removed from wave5_vpu_dec_close(): the integer inst_count and the struct vpu_instance *inst_elm pointer. No other code in the shown hunk was changed.
intent_record.how: This change does not alter runtime behavior directly in the visible hunk; it simply eliminates unused local declarations, reducing dead code and avoiding compiler warnings for unused variables.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove an incorrect autosuspend policy adjustment from decoder close so runtime PM behavior is no longer altered based on instance counting.
intent_record.what: The diff removes a `list_for_each_entry()` loop that counted `vpu_dev->instances`, along with the conditional call to `pm_runtime_dont_use_autosuspend(vpu_dev->dev)` when the count was 1, from `wave5_vpu_dec_close()`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, closing a decoder instance no longer changes the device's runtime PM autosuspend policy based on the number of active instances. The function now proceeds directly to unlock and drop the runtime PM reference without disabling autosuspend for the single-instance case.

intent_record.what: Two local variables, `int inst_count = 0;` and `struct vpu_instance *inst_elm;`, were removed from `wave5_vpu_enc_close(struct vpu_instance *inst, u32 *fail_res)`.
intent_record.how: This change does not alter runtime behavior by itself; it only eliminates unused declarations from the function body, so the function's execution logic remains the same.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove incorrect instance-count-based autosuspend handling from the encoder close path.
intent_record.what: The code removes a block from `wave5_vpu_enc_close()` that iterated over `vpu_dev->instances` to count instances and conditionally called `pm_runtime_dont_use_autosuspend(vpu_dev->dev)` when the count was 1.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the close path no longer changes the device's runtime PM autosuspend policy based on the number of active instances, so the function now just frees DMA memory, unlocks the hardware mutex, and drops the runtime PM reference.

Remove the first-instance autosuspend activation from decoder open handling.
Remove incorrect instance-count-based autosuspend handling from the encoder close path.
Increase the VPU runtime PM autosuspend delay from 100 to 500 to avoid suspending the device too aggressively.
Remove unused local variables from wave5_vpu_dec_close() to clean up the function.
Remove an incorrect autosuspend policy adjustment from decoder close so runtime PM behavior is no longer altered based on instance counting.

consistency_review.core_intent: Adjust runtime power management around destination buffer queuing for VPU decode handling.
consistency_review.reason: Hunk 1 is about putting the device back to autosuspend by releasing the PM reference after queueing, while Hunk 0 is about resuming the device before queueing; these are opposite PM actions and do not share a single coherent fix direction.

consistency_review.core_intent: Remove incorrect instance-count-based autosuspend handling from encoder lifecycle code.
consistency_review.reason: Hunk 8 targets fixing autosuspend logic in the close path based on instance count, while Hunk 3 removes a one-time autosuspend setup from the open path; these are related to runtime PM but address different code paths and changes, so they do not form a single tight coherent subset.

consistency_review.core_intent: Remove one-time autosuspend setup from codec open/registration paths so instance setup no longer alters runtime PM behavior.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly adjusts runtime-PM/autosuspend reference handling in the buffer queue path, which matches the root cause of the device autosuspending while decoder code still accesses hardware registers.

The changes directly modify runtime-PM/autosuspend setup tied to codec open/instance lifetime, which matches the root cause where incorrect autosuspend handling allowed hardware access after the device could suspend.

The change directly removes instance-count-based autosuspend handling, which matches the root cause of incorrect runtime-PM/autosuspend tied to instance lifetime. Even though the hunk is in the encoder close path, it addresses the same class of bug described in the vulnerability.

The root cause is incorrect runtime-PM/autosuspend timing causing the VPU to suspend while a buffer-queue path still touches hardware. Increasing the autosuspend delay directly changes that timing and is aimed at preventing premature suspension, so it is related to the vulnerability.

The change only removes unused સ્થાનિક variables in wave5_vpu_dec_close() and does not modify runtime-PM/autosuspend behavior, hardware register access, or the decoder queue path implicated in the SError.
The change directly targets the runtime-PM/autosuspend handling tied to decoder open/close lifecycle, which is the root cause of the hardware access during idle/closed transitions.

The change only removes unused local variables in the encoder close path and does not affect runtime-PM/autosuspend handling, decoder buffer queue access, or the `wave5_dec_clr_disp_flag()` hardware access that caused the SError.

The change directly addresses runtime-PM/autosuspend around the decoder buffer queue path by resuming the VPU before destination buffer handling, which matches the root cause where hardware registers were accessed after the device could autosuspend.

candidates.rationale: This pre-fix path queues a destination buffer without any explicit runtime-PM resume/power-hold around the queue operation, allowing later access to hardware registers while the device may already autosuspend.

This instance-count-based policy change in close handling incorrectly toggles autosuspend based on remaining instances, which is the root cause of the device being allowed to autosuspend at the wrong time.

The decoder close path also conditionally disables autosuspend based on instance count, contributing to incorrect runtime-PM state transitions that can leave hardware inaccessible during buffer handling.

Enabling autosuspend from decoder open based on the first instance ties PM policy to instance lifetime, which is the underlying misuse that can let the device suspend while later buffer-queue code still needs it.
The encoder open path makes the same incorrect one-time autosuspend setup tied to instance registration, demonstrating the faulty PM policy pattern that can trigger premature suspend.

vuln_statements.explanation: This runtime-PM policy change is tied to decoder instance open/close lifetime, which is the root cause of the device being allowed to autosuspend at the wrong time while later decoder buffer-queue paths still access hardware registers.

This close-path autosuspend toggle depends on remaining instance count rather than actual hardware activity, creating incorrect runtime-PM transitions that can let the VPU suspend while decoder cleanup or buffer handling still needs register access.

This destination-buffer queue operation lacks an explicit runtime-PM resume or power hold around the queueing path, so it can proceed into later hardware register access after the device has autosuspended.
This encoder open path shows the same incorrect instance-lifetime-based autosuspend setup pattern, demonstrating the faulty PM policy that can trigger premature suspend of the shared device.
